claims.text: Traditional EAM reference potentials insufficiently represent the configurational diversity of high-entropy-alloy liquids.
An actively learned deep neural network potential can be constructed from ab initio data for use as a thermodynamic-integration reference.
Replacing an EAM reference with the deep-learning potential will improve reference–ab initio phase-space overlap.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The intervention is applicable to high-entropy alloys and complex concentrated alloys near their melting points, approximately 0.9–1.1 Tm.
High-temperature high-entropy-alloy liquids contain many coexisting local atomic environments and substantial configurational diversity.
The deep-learning potential encodes the relevant many-body interactions and diversity of local atomic environments.
Encoding those interactions and environments produces a reference ensemble that samples liquid configuration space more accurately.
Machine-learned potentials can be trained on ab initio data spanning varied atomic environments.
A deep-learning potential can represent both solid and liquid phases of a high-entropy material.
The trained deep-learning potential will reproduce the ab initio potential-energy surface of both solid and liquid alloy phases more faithfully than an EAM potential.
Closer reproduction of the ab initio potential-energy surface will tighten reference–target ensemble matching and minimize integration-path mismatch.
The intervention may reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately a factor of 2–10.
The magnitude of improvement depends on alloy composition, temperature, and training-data quality.
The method requires sufficient ab initio training data and manageable computational cost.
The potential may fail under extreme conditions or outside the environments represented in its training data.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing EAM-reference and deep-learning-reference thermodynamic integration for the same alloy and temperature.
The hypothesis is falsified if the deep-learning reference gives overlap, convergence, and free-energy-path metrics comparable to or worse than the EAM reference.
